ig_pack.note: Instagram is a re-cut feeder, not the goal. Never let an Instagram result set YouTube strategy (CHANNEL-PERFORMANCE.md §3.5). No retention curve, no CTR, no search terms exist on this platform.

do_more_do_less.action: Stop making posts that get shared without converting
do_more_do_less.evidence: 18 of 104 rated posts are shared above the median (24.7/1k) but convert below it (2.0/1k): median 9.8k reach for a median 9 followers. The 34 posts that do both average 275 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen.

do_more_do_less.action: Write carousels in the revision lane
do_more_do_less.evidence: 50 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 20 for the other lanes (41 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 10.8k, conversion 3.77 vs 1.95 per 1k.

The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 33 followers (91 posts); outside the band, 12 (16 posts). Pooled rate 2.89 vs 1.85 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact.
87 single images all time: 84.2k reach between them and 120 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 159.6. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken.

do_more_do_less.action: Stop reading the reach number as a result
do_more_do_less.evidence: Across the 16 posts that passed 100k reach, conversion runs 0.03 to 10.31 follows per 1k — a 395x spread at comparable reach, which is the proof that reach is not what is being measured. Worst: 804.9k reach for 21 followers — "@bhuvan.bam22 one of the most recognisable faces in Indian p". Best: 112.6k reach for 1161 — "Before the seventh century, the Arabian Peninsula was home t". The smaller post took 55x more followers on 7x less reach. Judge a post on follows; reach only sizes the room it was shown in.

do_more_do_less.action: Stop opening reels on freedom-movement framing
do_more_do_less.evidence: 21 freedom-lane reels: median skip 59.6%, against the 45% gate, and 1 of them passed 20,000 reach. The revision lane's reels reach a median 2.5k. Reels report no follows at all, so reach is the only thing measurable here — and this lane does not get it.

scenario_calibration.note: The last 3 mature months averaged 2,270 follows against a modelled 2,351, within 15%. The model tracks reality.

scenario_assumptions: Feed only. Instagram reports `follows` on carousels and images and NEVER on reels, so the 231 reels on this account contribute an unmeasured number of followers on top. Every figure here is a LOWER BOUND on total growth.

Baseline is the 110 feed posts published between 21 and 180 days ago. Younger posts are excluded because `follows` is a lifetime counter and there is only one insights snapshot, so their totals are still accruing.
Cadence held at the observed 21.1 feed posts a month except in the third scenario.

"Expected" uses mean follows per post and therefore assumes breakouts keep happening at the observed rate — the top 10 posts in the baseline carry 56% of its followers. "Floor" uses medians and is what a month with no breakout yields. The truth is usually nearer the floor plus one good post.
Per-cell rates are assumed stable under a mix change. If the revision lane's reach is partly novelty, pushing it to 80% of output will regress toward the floor row, not the expected row.
No seasonality adjustment; the baseline is a single 180-day window.
thin_data: **Single image** has only 3 posts in the baseline window. Its median of 1 follows is a sample, not a rate.
**freedom lane** has only 4 feed posts in the baseline window — not enough to advise for or against it.
**1-card band**: 3 posts. Reported for completeness only.
**2-4-card band**: 3 posts. Reported for completeness only.
**5-6-card band**: 6 posts. Reported for completeness only.
**11+-card band**: 7 posts. Reported for completeness only.

**Recent posts cannot be judged yet.** The 11 feed posts under 21 days old show 137.6k reach for 448 follows (3.26/1k) against a baseline of 2.84/1k. There is exactly one insights snapshot in the database, so this cannot be split between follows still accruing and a genuine decline. Re-fetch insights in two to three weeks and compare; if the gap holds, it is real.

**231 reels carry no conversion data at all.** Instagram does not report `follows` on reels, so their contribution to the follower count is unknown and is excluded from every projection. The projections are therefore lower bounds.

not_transferable_to_youtube.why_not: A carousel swipe has no YouTube analogue. It is not chapters, not a playlist, not retention.

Instagram reach and YouTube impressions are different denominators over different audiences. YouTube's subs-per-1k-views is computed separately in the YouTube modules and the two must never be pooled.

not_transferable_to_youtube.finding: Any single post's reach, including the 802,709-reach carousel
not_transferable_to_youtube.why_not: An Instagram hit is not evidence a topic is hot on YouTube. The same script did 47,669 on Instagram and 14 on YouTube; across 36 dual-published scripts r = -0.10.
Instagram's 3-second swipe-away. The YouTube Analytics API does not expose it, and the stay-at-3s proxy the Shorts tracker uses passes every Short, so the numbers are not comparable.
Shares are the Instagram feed's distribution engine. YouTube has no equivalent mechanism and no per-video share rate worth ranking on.

not_transferable_to_youtube.finding: Instagram growth as a reason to make anything for YouTube
not_transferable_to_youtube.why_not: Instagram sends YouTube roughly 378 views a year. It is a parallel audience, not a feeder, so no Instagram number may appear in a YouTube recommendation's justification.

not_transferable_to_youtube.finding: The revision lane (a partial exception, stated so it is not over-applied)
not_transferable_to_youtube.why_not: The revision lane does also win on YouTube long-form, but that was measured independently on YouTube data in src/instagram/bridge.ts. It is a coincidence of two separate findings, not a transfer. Individual scripts still do not carry across.

growth.note: INSTAGRAM ONLY. No YouTube figure was used to build this section and none of it may justify a YouTube recommendation: across 36 dual-published scripts the platforms correlate at r = -0.10, and Instagram sends YouTube about 378 views a year. Ranked on followers, never reach; reach and growth are near-uncorrelated on this account (0.02 to 17.0 follows per 1k among posts over 20k reach). All projections are feed-attributed and are lower bounds, because Instagram reports no `follows` on reels.
